links.outcome: e-Stroke performance on local prospective cohort against neuroradiologist ground truth
links.effect: e-ASPECTS accuracy 77.0% (specificity 83.5%, sensitivity 58.6%); hyperdense thrombus accuracy 69.1%, PPV 22.9%; haemorrhage accuracy 97.8%; e-CTA LVO accuracy 91.5%.
links.quote: For identifying acute middle cerebral artery territory ischaemia, e-ASPECTS had an accuracy of 77.0% and was more specific (83.5%) than sensitive (58.6%).

links.outcome: Accuracy limits of AI imaging output relevant to use as stand-alone diagnosis
links.effect: Hyperdense thrombus PPV was 22.9% with many false positives; e-ASPECTS sensitivity 58.6%; authors conclude it should be an adjunct to expert interpretation, not standalone.
links.quote: The accuracy for identifying hyperdense thrombus was lower (69.1%), which was mainly due to many false positives (positive predictive value of 22.9%).

screen.reason: Prospective real-world clinical evaluation of an AI-based acute stroke CT decision support tool (Brainomix e-Stroke) assessing diagnostic accuracy and processing time on unselected consecutive patients.
